- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: 3299-3305 (merge-base fetch)
  Problem: `git merge-base` output is not constrained to a single hash; criss-cross histories can cause multiple hashes to be captured in `merge_base`.
  Why it fails at runtime: A multi-line `merge_base` can be passed to `git rev-parse`, causing downstream hash lookups to fail silently, incorrectly skipping refresh.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: 3341-3354 (divergence check)
  Problem: `_int_short` and `_base_short` are declared with `local` inside the `if` block, which may mislead maintainers into thinking they are block-scoped, but Bash `local` is function-scoped; under `set -u` or explicit strictness, this can expose unbound-variable hazards.
  Why it fails at runtime: In the current code it works, but the placement is confusing and technically unsafe if the `if` branch is entered without `base_hash` assigned.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: 3335-3345 (base_hash lookup)
  Problem: `base_hash` is unconditionally used in the divergence comparison even when `git rev-parse --verify --quiet` returns an empty string, making "file missing at merge-base" indistinguishable from a transient lookup failure.
  Why it fails at runtime: In fetch-race or unreachable-merge-base scenarios, the deadlock-breaker can be suppressed unintentionally.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===
- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: 3312-3314, 3353
  Problem: `git merge-base` without `--all` can theoretically return multiple hashes in criss-cross merge scenarios, which would cause `base_hash` lookup to fail or behave unexpectedly when the multi-line value is passed to `git rev-parse "${merge_base}:${f}"`.
  Why it fails at runtime: While standard `git merge-base` (without `--all`) returns a single "best" common ancestor, in complex criss-cross merge histories there can be multiple merge bases. The code assumes a single hash value. If git were to return multiple lines (either through unusual repository state or future git version changes), the subsequent `git rev-parse` command would receive a multi-line value, causing the lookup to fail and `base_hash` to become empty, potentially triggering incorrect divergence detection.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2

- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: 3312-3314, 3356-3357 (2 related items)
  Problem: Suggested minimal fixes: add `| head -n 1` to the `merge_base` assignment and move `local _int_short` / `local _base_short` out of the conditional block.
  Why: These are hardening suggestions for the same areas called out in the review.

=== FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_20 ===
- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: 3309-3312 (merge_base=...) and 3339-3343 (base_hash lookup + comparison)
  Problem: `git merge-base` (without --all) is captured verbatim. In complex histories it can emit multiple newline-separated SHAs; the later `git rev-parse "${merge_base}:${f}"` receives a multi-line value, causing base_hash="" on every file and forcing the divergence-skip path even for legitimate deadlock-breaker cases.
  Why it fails at runtime: The no-clobber guard triggers on every drifted allowlisted file when the worktree's history contains criss-cross merges or multiple common ancestors, silently suppressing refreshes that the function was added to perform. The two behavioural tests only exercise linear histories.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: 3349-3354 (local _int_short=... inside if)
  Problem: The two `local` declarations and the subsequent short-hash logic live inside the per-file `if [ -n "${merge_base}" ]` block; they are unreachable when merge_base is empty (the exact fail-open case the preceding warning documents).
  Why it fails at runtime: When merge-base resolution fails the skip log line is never printed, making it impossible for operators to distinguish intentional no-op from a lookup failure. The zero-refresh summary logic also never sees skipped_count incremented.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: 3297-3305 (the single merge_base lookup before the for-loop)
  Problem: The merge-base is resolved on the detached worktree created from the integration_branch ref, but the worktree creation itself (lines ~3285) uses a bare `git worktree add` with no `--force` or post-creation `git fetch` guarantee. A concurrent push to origin can make the remote ref stale before the merge-base query runs.
  Why it fails at runtime: base_hash becomes based on an out-of-date common ancestor, causing false-positive divergence skips on files changed only on default_branch. The later behavioural test fixture never races the bare repo, so the race is un-covered.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

- File: tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py
  Line or code reference: 8088-8115 (_extract_refresh_function_body + depth counter)
  Problem: The brace-depth parser treats any top-level `function() {` as a nesting increase but stops at the first `}` that brings depth to zero. The test fixture runner sources the extracted substring as a standalone function; any future inner command-group `{ ... }` or nested function definition that happens to line up with the strip() logic will truncate the body, making the static guard test pass on an incomplete function.
  Why it fails at runtime: A later innocent formatting change or added helper inside _refresh_integration_resolver_tooling silently turns the regression test into a no-op (fn_body no longer contains the guard), allowing the original #2734 regression to reappear undetected.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

- File: probably_unnecessary_but_read_if_stuck.md
  Line or code reference: ~222 (allowlist paragraph updated in LAST RUN DIFF)
  Problem: The documentation was updated to list `scripts/targeted_file_context.py` and the timeout-prelude, but the live `refresh_files=(...)` array in orchestrate_poll_process.sh (and the consumer-repo cleanup block in line ~10400) still reference the canonical list. The docs and code have drifted again immediately after the previous autofix pass that attempted to sync them.
  Why it fails at runtime: Operator documentation no longer matches the contract enforced by heal_integration_branch_conflict and the post-merge cleanup, leading to false expectations about which files survive the [ai-maint] refresh on orchestrator/project-* branches.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_20 ===
